# Question Answering Skill

## Workflow

1. **Name the answer slot.** Decide what kind of thing the question asks for:
   the head noun after "this"/"these" ("this U.S. territory", "these animals",
   "this type of chewing gum") or the gap a definition leaves open. Treat that
   head noun as a hard constraint on the answer.
2. **Classify the clue.**
   - *Description or definition*: the answer is whatever the description
     defines.
   - *"this X" / "these Xs"*: the answer is an X. A related organization,
     institution, work, or title that merely contains X is not an X.
   - *Named trio* ("A, B, C"): the three items share one property; answer with
     the conventional single-noun label for that property, not a descriptive
     sentence.
   - *Multiple choice* ("of 2, 5, or 10"): answer with one listed option,
     nothing else.
3. **Draft the shortest complete answer.** Pick the specific term the clue
   points to rather than a generic restatement of the question, then strip
   everything that is not the answer: no parenthetical alternatives, no "or"
   lists of other possibilities, no extra qualifiers. For a person, give the
   name as the person is usually known, not a fully expanded formal name, and
   answer with the part of the name the clue did not supply: when the clue
   names only the forename, answer with the surname alone; when the clue
   writes out the full name, give that exact form back, adding no middle
   initials or extra forenames.
   Do not re-attach the category the clue already named: when the clue says
   "this island", "this company", or "this term", and the distinctive word is
   a complete recognizable name on its own, answer with that word alone. Keep
   the category word only when the distinctive part is an adjective that
   cannot stand alone ("Roman Empire", "drip irrigation") or when the answer
   is a work's title ("Gorky Park").
4. **Verify against the slot.** Say "The answer is a ___", filling the slot
   from step 1 with your draft. If the sentence reads wrong, the draft is the
   wrong kind of entity or the wrong level of generality — redraft. Then run
   the category check: if a word in your draft is exactly the category word
   the clue already supplied for the slot ("this market" -> market, "this
   vitamin" -> vitamin), delete that word and answer with the distinguishing
   remainder ("bear", "C"). Put the word back only when the whole phrase is
   the established name ("South Sea Bubble", "Roman Empire", "Ace Hardware").
5. **Emit** only the final string inside `<answer>...</answer>`.

## Error Avoidance

- Answer the slot, not the surrounding entity. A clue asking for a territory
  wants the territory, not the university located in it; a clue asking for a
  type of business wants the business type, not the name of the businesses'
  alliance.
- Exactly one answer form. A parenthetical or slash alternative ("X (also Y)")
  breaks exact match even when one form is right, and so does an appended
  example or hedge list ("X or Y, occasionally Z").
- Name the specific variety when the clue asks for a type or kind; answering
  with the generic category plus an adjective misses the target.
- Match the conventional form. Prefer the short form the answer is normally
  called (a plural noun for a class of cities, the standard one-word term for
  a technology or a sport — "hockey", not "ice hockey") over a longer phrase
  that means the same thing. For a person,
  use the customary short or nickname form — don't stack every forename, and
  don't substitute a formal given name for a common nickname. For a place, a
  company, or a term, give the distinctive name on its own rather than naming
  the category again: "Roanoke" not "Roanoke Island", "Hallmark" not
  "Hallmark Cards", "transit" not "Transit of Venus" — but keep the category
  in "Roman Empire" and "drip irrigation", where the distinctive word cannot
  stand alone. Trimming stops at the complete conventional name: keep a
  regnal numeral ("Richard III"), a title that belongs to the familiar name
  ("Sir Isaac Newton"), and the second half of a compound proper name
  ("Funk & Wagnalls"). These identify which entity is meant; they are not
  extra qualifiers. By the same measure, never attach the relation or the
  kind of item to an answer that is already complete: for a list of people
  who were all someone's spouses, answer with that person's name alone, not
  the name plus "'s wives"; for a list of characters, answer with the work's
  title alone, not the title plus "characters".

abbreviation-expanded-vs-abbreviated.description: Agent writes the feature designator out in full ('Mount') where the gold uses the conventional abbreviation ('Mt.').
abbreviation-expanded-vs-abbreviated.evidence: Trajectory [4]: 'this mountain near Los Angeles ... home to a famous observatory' answered 'Mount Wilson' (F1 0.5); the gold is 'Mt. Wilson'.
abbreviation-expanded-vs-abbreviated.label: abbreviation-expanded-vs-abbreviated

answer-fragment-missing-verb.description: Agent answers with the noun fragment ('state's evidence') where the gold retains the leading verb of the idiom ('turn state's evidence').
answer-fragment-missing-verb.evidence: Trajectory [30]: '"Turning" this type of "evidence"' answered 'state's evidence' (F1 0.8); the gold is the 3-token 'turn state's evidence'. Likely gold-form annotation variance, opposite direction from the accepted trim floor.
answer-fragment-missing-verb.label: answer-fragment-missing-verb

attempts.approach: Same patch adds "keep a title that belongs to the familiar name ('Sir Isaac Newton')" to rule 5, supplying an honorific-retention floor.

answer-name-missing-honorific.description: Agent gives the plain name where the gold retains an honorific prefix, missing exact match; conflicts with the short-form pressure applied for the other name case.
answer-name-missing-honorific.evidence: Trajectory [16]: "president of the Royal Society in 1703 ... until his death in 1727" → "Isaac Newton" (F1=0.800, EM=0) where the gold keeps the honorific ("Sir Isaac Newton") — the exact case the iter_10 honorific-retention floor in rule 5 was written to cover.
answer-name-missing-honorific.examples_state_evidence: Rule 5 attaches the concrete example 'a title that belongs to the familiar name ('Sir Isaac Newton')', directly illustrating honorific retention.
answer-name-missing-honorific.label: answer-name-missing-honorific

attempts.approach: Extended Error Avoidance rule 5's short-form preference to cover sports, adding the concrete pair 'hockey', not 'ice hockey'.

answer-over-specified-with-extra-modifie.description: Agent answers the sport with the two-word variant 'ice hockey' where the conventional one-word form 'hockey' is the gold, adding a qualifier the clue never used.
answer-over-specified-with-extra-modifie.evidence: Trajectory [16]: clue 'perform a hat trick ... in this sport' answered 'ice hockey' (EM 0, F1 0.667); the gold is the single token 'hockey'.
answer-over-specified-with-extra-modifie.label: answer-over-specified-with-extra-modifier

answer-synonym-differs-from-gold.description: For a definitional clue the agent gives a true synonym of the intended term while the gold uses the other common name, giving zero exact match.
answer-synonym-differs-from-gold.evidence: Trajectory [28]: "A larval toad or frog" -> "Tadpole" (EM=0, F1=0.000); the gold shares no token with 'tadpole', i.e. the other common name for a larval amphibian is expected.
answer-synonym-differs-from-gold.label: answer-synonym-differs-from-gold

attempts.approach: Appended a floor to rule 5 ("Match the conventional form"): trimming stops at the complete conventional name — keep a regnal numeral ("Richard III"), and the second half of a compound proper name ("Funk & Wagnalls"). Targets the over-trimming root cause seen in [2] and [25].

Revises the step-4 category check to delete the clue-supplied word only when the remainder is itself a name/noun ("bear", "Roanoke"), keeping it when the remainder is a common adjective that needs the category noun ("pituitary gland", "eucalyptus tree") or when the whole phrase is the established name.
Replaces Workflow step 4's unconditional mechanical deletion of the clue-supplied category word with a nuanced keep-or-drop comparison, removing the over-trim mechanism.

answer-trimmed-below-gold-including-cate.description: The agent deletes the clue-supplied category noun from a two-word answer whose conventional form keeps it, because Workflow step 4's mechanical deletion command is unconditional; the gold is the fuller phrase.
answer-trimmed-below-gold-including-cate.evidence: Trajectory [18]: "In humans, muscles are defined as striated, cardiac or this type" -> "smooth" (EM=0, F1=0.667, which forces a 2-token gold containing 'smooth', i.e. "smooth muscle"). The step-4 category check was applied literally, and that deletion is exactly what removed the needed word.
answer-trimmed-below-gold-including-cate.examples_state_evidence: Rule 5 attaches concrete keep-forms 'Richard III', 'Sir Isaac Newton', 'Funk & Wagnalls', and Workflow step 3 names keep-cases 'Roman Empire', 'drip irrigation', directly illustrating when not to strip the category word.
answer-trimmed-below-gold-including-cate.label: answer-trimmed-below-gold-including-category

answered-with-description-not-entity.description: For a bare fragment/name clue the agent answers with a descriptive phrase instead of the specific entity the clue names.
answered-with-description-not-entity.evidence: Trajectory [10]: clue "The Beretta" → "Italian firearms manufacturing company"; zero token overlap with gold.
answered-with-description-not-entity.label: answered-with-description-not-entity

clue-referent-inference-mismatch.description: On a "multi-this" wordplay clue the agent answers with the complete compound word it already partly supplied instead of only the missing part that fills the "this" slot, yielding zero overlap.
clue-referent-inference-mismatch.evidence: Trajectory [14]: "A polyglot, one who speaks many languages, can also be called multi-this, from the Latin for 'tongue'" -> "multilingual" (EM=0, F1=0.000). The clue already supplied "multi-", so the slot wanted only "lingual".
clue-referent-inference-mismatch.label: clue-referent-inference-mismatch

common-name-vs-official-gold.description: Agent gives the common short country name where the gold carries the full official name.
common-name-vs-official-gold.evidence: Trajectory [5]: "Asia's population giant, finally admitted to U.N. in 1971" -> answered "China" vs gold "People's Republic of China" (EM=0, F1=0.4; one predicted token matching a 4-token gold).
common-name-vs-official-gold.label: common-name-vs-official-gold

example-answer-for-definition-clue.description: For a definitional clue ("a/an ___ that does ___"), the agent names an example/member of the class instead of the defined term itself.
example-answer-for-definition-clue.evidence: Trajectory [26]: "An astringent applied under the arms to curtail sweating" answered with the example "witch hazel" instead of the defined term "antiperspirant"; F1=0.
example-answer-for-definition-clue.label: example-answer-for-definition-clue
example-answer-for-definition-clue.resolve_evidence: Batch shows definitional clues answered with the defined term rather than an example/member: [6] "This industrial unit is equal to the work one person can do in 60 minutes" -> "man-hour"; [26] "Term for an international match..." -> "Test"; [28] "A 'hasty' dessert, or perhaps you'd prefer the tapioca" -> "pudding". Each gives the defined term, not a listed example.

attempts.approach: Added Error Avoidance items 'One answer only' (no parenthetical or slash alternative) and 'No example lists or hedges', plus Workflow step 3 stripping parentheticals and or-lists during drafting.

Extended rule 5 ('Match the conventional form') to require a work's title in one form only and forbid joining an original title to its translated/alternate title ("Il Postino", not "Il Postino: The Postman").

extra-alternatives-in-answer.description: Agent gives a second, colon-joined form of a work's title (original plus translated title) instead of a single title form.
extra-alternatives-in-answer.evidence: Trajectory [5]: "Poet Pablo Neruda befriends the title character of this recent film set in Italy" -> "Il Postino: The Postman"; gold is "Il Postino" (EM=0, F1=0.80 from the extra "The Postman" tokens). The agent attached the translated title to the original title, creating a second answer form.
extra-alternatives-in-answer.examples_state_evidence: The 'Exactly one answer form' item shows only placeholder templates 'X (also Y)' and 'X or Y, occasionally Z'; no concrete real-word correct/incorrect pair is attached under it.
extra-alternatives-in-answer.label: extra-alternatives-in-answer
extra-alternatives-in-answer.resolve_evidence: Trajectory [26]: title-translation clue ("My No. 1 country hit 'Mi Vida Loca' translates to this in English") answered with the single form "My Crazy Life" — no original-plus-translation join — matching gold (EM=1). The scenario that previously produced "Il Postino: The Postman" triggered and was handled correctly.

full-name-answered-when-gold-is-surname.description: Agent answers the full personal name where the gold carries only the surname.
full-name-answered-when-gold-is-surname.evidence: Trajectory [28]: "this Arkansan said..." → "Mike Huckabee"; gold "Huckabee" (F1=0.667, one of two tokens matched).
full-name-answered-when-gold-is-surname.label: full-name-answered-when-gold-is-surname
full-name-answered-when-gold-is-surname.resolve_evidence: Trajectory [20]: clue asks for 'this Lake Poet' who visited Sir Walter Scott in 1803; the gold is the surname 'Wordsworth' and the agent answers the surname alone, not a full expanded name (EM 1.0).

attempts.approach: Added Error Avoidance item 'Name the specific variety when the clue asks for a type or kind' and Workflow step 3 instructing the agent to pick the specific term rather than a generic restatement.

generic-category-instead-of-specific-typ.description: When the clue asks for a type or kind, the agent answers with the generic category plus a modifier rather than naming the specific variety.
generic-category-instead-of-specific-typ.evidence: Trajectory 3 (a234f472): 'Rubber is an ingredient in this type of chewing gum' → 'Modern chewing gum' (EM=0, F1=0.4; the specific variety 'bubble gum' is the target, and the adjective 'Modern' is dead weight).
generic-category-instead-of-specific-typ.label: generic-category-instead-of-specific-type
generic-category-instead-of-specific-typ.resolve_evidence: Type-of clues are triggered and answered with the specific variety: Trajectory [19] "one of these bombs" → "hydrogen bomb"; Trajectory [30] "get one of these ... shoulders pinned" → "fall"; Trajectory [9] "a term for a free-form musical composition" → "Rhapsody". No case answered with a generic category + modifier.

hero-entity-instead-of-work-title.description: On a plot-description clue the agent names the epic's protagonist instead of the work's title.
hero-entity-instead-of-work-title.evidence: Trajectory [29]: "700 B.C.: Greek warrior takes epic 10-year journey to get home" answered "Odysseus"; gold is the work title (Odyssey) — zero token overlap because the person was named instead of the work.
hero-entity-instead-of-work-title.label: hero-entity-instead-of-work-title
hero-entity-instead-of-work-title.resolve_evidence: Trajectory [7]: character-description clue ("a transvestite street drummer named Angel ... in this long-running musical") answered with the work title "Rent", not the character. Trajectory [27]: "this series ended with J.R.'s brother Bobby getting shot" answered "Dallas", not a character. Trajectory [14]: book-topic clue answered "Friday Night Lights". The protagonist-instead-of-title failure did not recur across multiple work-identifying clues.

historical-name-vs-current-name.description: For a landmark identified by a historical/touristic detail, the agent answers with the modern current name where the gold carries the historically contemporaneous name.
historical-name-vs-current-name.evidence: Trajectory [17]: '6925 Hollywood Blvd... Hands, feet, cement' answered 'TCL Chinese Theatre' where gold is 'Grauman's Chinese Theatre' (EM=0, F1=0.333, only 'Chinese' overlaps) — current corporate name chosen over the historical name.
historical-name-vs-current-name.label: historical-name-vs-current-name

knowledge-miss-zero-overlap.description: Agent answers a plausible but wrong animal on a knowledge/photo clue, sharing no token with the gold.
knowledge-miss-zero-overlap.evidence: Trajectory [27]: 'this predator that comes in gray and red types' answered 'fox' with F1 0.0 — the gold is a different animal.
knowledge-miss-zero-overlap.label: knowledge-miss-zero-overlap

attempts.approach: Added Workflow step 2 ('Named trio → answer with the conventional single-noun label, not a descriptive sentence') and Error Avoidance item 'Match the conventional label' preferring the short standard form.

non-canonical-label-for-trio.description: For a bare comma-separated list of three names the agent answers with the group the names belong to ("The Rolling Stones") instead of the conventional single-noun label of the shared property, giving zero token overlap.
non-canonical-label-for-trio.evidence: Trajectory [9]: "Mick Jagger,Keith Richards,Charlie Watts" -> "The Rolling Stones" (EM=0, F1=0.000). With article-stripping the predicted tokens are 'rolling stones', and the zero overlap proves the gold contains neither, i.e. the expected form was not the band name but the shared-property label.

official-name-instead-of-conventional.description: Agent renders a government department's formal full name ("Department of the Treasury") where the conventional short form ("Treasury Department") is the gold.
official-name-instead-of-conventional.evidence: Trajectory [29] ("This cabinet department is in charge of the enforcement of Prohibition"): answered "Department of the Treasury" vs conventional "Treasury Department" (EM=0, F1=0.8).
official-name-instead-of-conventional.label: official-name-instead-of-conventional

attempts.approach: Added person-name guidance to Workflow step 3 ('give the name as the person is usually known, not a fully expanded formal name') and revised rule 5 into 'Match the conventional form' with person specifics (don't stack every forename; don't substitute a formal given name for a common nickname).
Extended the person-name guidance in Workflow step 3: if the clue already writes the name, reuse that exact form rather than expanding it with added middle initials or forenames.

attempts.approach: Added a conditional to Workflow step 3 and Error Avoidance rule 5: strip the category word the clue already supplied when the distinctive part is a standalone name ("Hallmark", "Roanoke", "transit"), but keep it when the distinctive part is an adjective that cannot stand alone ("Roman Empire", "drip irrigation") or the answer is a work's title.

Added a mechanical category check to Workflow step 4: if a draft word is exactly the category word the clue supplied for the slot, delete it and answer with the remainder, restoring it only when the whole phrase is the established name ("South Sea Bubble", "Roman Empire", "Ace Hardware").

Extended Workflow step 4 with a superset check: drop an unrequested descriptive modifier when the plain headword is the term ('balloon', not 'speech balloon') and answer with the named people/things when the draft is a containing work's title ('these exiles').

Widened the step-4 mechanical deletion check to drop any word the clue already contains (clue-supplied modifiers like 'funeral' -> pyre, and clue-written surnames on moniker clues -> moniker alone), not just the exact category word, and expanded the restore carve-outs to established-name forms (South Sea Bubble, Roman Empire, Ace Hardware, drip irrigation, Gorky Park).

Same patch attempts to distinguish drop cases ("Doppler", "Hallmark", "Roanoke") from keep cases ("timing gun", "pituitary gland", "Beaufort scale") instead of mechanically stripping the category word.

redundant-class-word-appended.description: Agent appends the clue-supplied class word to a distinctive answer that stands alone, so the answer no longer matches the shorter gold.

Trajectory [22]: clue says 'this state university at Superior', yet answered 'University of Wisconsin-Superior', re-attaching the category/university word.

The drop behaviour works elsewhere in the same batch — [30] "lily", [19] "Camembert", [13] "cornea" all dropped the clue-supplied category word correctly — so this is a failure to apply the existing drop rule, not a missing one.
redundant-class-word-appended.examples_state_evidence: Error Avoidance rule 5 contains concrete correct/incorrect pairs directly addressing redundant class-word appending: "Roanoke" not "Roanoke Island", "Hallmark" not "Hallmark Cards", "transit" not "Transit of Venus".

redundant-class-word-appended.resolve_evidence: Trajectories [11] ('this ... island' -> 'New Zealand', not 'New Zealand island'), [17] ('this place' -> 'Chaillot', not 'Chaillot place'), [10] ('this black candy' -> 'Licorice'): in each the clue supplies a class word and the agent answers with only the distinctive name, matching the gold.

attempts.approach: Added Workflow steps 1 and 4 (name the head noun after 'this'/'these' as a hard slot constraint and verify by substituting into 'The answer is a ___') plus an Error Avoidance item 'Answer the slot, not the surrounding entity'.

slot-entity-mismatch.description: Agent answers with the document/work associated with the asked-for person instead of the person who occupies the answer slot.
slot-entity-mismatch.evidence: Trajectory [4] (0fe06452): clue "On June 16, 1881 he wrote an explanation of why he was going to kill President Garfield" asks for the writer (a person); the agent answered "Address to the American People", the title of what that person wrote — EM=0, F1=0. This recurs the mode fixed earlier by the 'Answer the slot, not the surrounding entity' item.
slot-entity-mismatch.label: slot-entity-mismatch
slot-entity-mismatch.resolve_evidence: Person-slot clues that mention associated works were answered with the person, not the work: [4] "wrote… before hitting it big with 'I, the Jury'" -> Mickey Spillane; [27] "'The Queen of Spades' by this composer" -> Tchaikovsky (composer, not opera); [14] -> Olivia Newton-John. The slot discipline now holds.

title-subtitle-over-specified.description: Agent keeps a work's subtitle / long-form title where the gold is the short title alone.
title-subtitle-over-specified.evidence: Trajectory [20]: late-night sketch-comedy show -> answered "Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip" (5 tokens after article-strip) vs gold "Studio 60" (EM=0, F1=0.571).
title-subtitle-over-specified.label: title-subtitle-over-specified

trio-identities-wrong-property.description: For a bare comma-separated list of names, the agent supplies a wrong shared-property label because it mis-identifies the common property.
trio-identities-wrong-property.evidence: Trajectory [2]: query "Edward Kennedy,John Kerry" answered "Senators"; gold shares no tokens (F1=0.0), so the intended shared property differs — a knowledge/inference miss rather than a formatting failure.
trio-identities-wrong-property.label: trio-identities-wrong-property
trio-identities-wrong-property.resolve_evidence: Trajectory [12]: "Panne, cut & crushed are types of this thick pile fabric" -> "velvet" (EM=1, F1=1.0).
